intro_cards.title: About these notes
body: 8 units · tectonics to contours

Grade 12 is “geography of Eritrea in depth”. Grade 11 is the toolkit: how the crust moves, how water and wind carve, how people settle, then a first look at Eritrea’s place, relief and contour maps. Read each unit as a *story with a cause* — examiners mark the cause, not only the landform name.

intro_cards.title: Worked contour gradient
body: Two points: 1 200 m and 1 000 m. Map distance between them is 4 cm. Scale 1:50 000 (1 cm = 500 m).
Rise = 200 m. Run = 4 × 500 = 2 000 m. Gradient = 200/2000 = 1 in 10 (or 10%). Write both the fraction and a sentence: “For every 10 m walked horizontally you climb 1 m.”

units.title: Map Work: Landforms on Contour Maps
units.intro: A **contour line** joins every point that is the same height above a datum (usually sea level). The map does not show every metre — it samples at a fixed **contour interval** (e.g. 20 m). Read the printed numbers; never

cards.title: 8.1 Major Land forms on Maps
body: Hill: A hill is an area of land usually rounded in shape that is higher than the surrounding areas.
A hill has a broad base and is almost circular in shape.

cards.title: Reading contours

cards.title: Contours & landforms
body: Contour = equal elevation. Spot heights, layer colouring, hachures.
Valley: contours V upstream. Ridge: opposite. Cliff: lines merge.

cards.title: Cross-sections
body: Draw line on map; transfer contour heights to graph axes.
Vertical exaggeration makes relief readable.

cards.title: 8.2 Minor Land forms on Maps
body: A single type of a major land form may contain one or more types of minor land forms.
A mountain ridge, for example, may include many other minor land features. due to external and internal forces.

cards.title: 8.3 Gradients and Cross Sections
body: Gradient expresses the ratio of change in the altitude of a slope.
In other words, it expresses the ratio between vertical distance and horizontal distance.

questions.q: [Contour map, see Fig. 1 (image).] The highest point on the map is indicated by letter
why: E lies inside three closed contours that are themselves inside the contour labelled 1600 m, so E is above 1900 m (1700, 1800, 1900 loops).
Counting outwards from C to the same contour that bends at L gives fewer lines than from E, so hill C is lower; P and H have only two small loops each and G is a saddle.
